posts.text:
The world has already consumed nearly 1 BILLION barrels of its oil inventory buffer.

At today's ADIPEC conference, ADNOC CEO Sultan Al Jaber revealed three extraordinary developments in the physical oil market.

1. Nearly 1 billion barrels have been drawn from global oil inventories to absorb supply disruptions.

2. Diesel inventories in some markets have fallen to their lowest seasonal levels in 35 years.

3. Logistics costs, which previously accounted for less than 5% of a barrel's cost, now account for more than 30%.

The implications are significant.

The world has been absorbing supply disruptions by drawing down inventories rather than through a full adjustment in demand. This has helped cushion the immediate impact on oil prices, but that buffer is being depleted.

Meanwhile, diesel inventories are already critically tight in some markets, and the cost of transporting oil has exploded. Even when crude is physically available, getting it to the right market is becoming increasingly expensive.

This is creating a dangerous combination of shrinking inventories, tightening refined product supplies and rising logistical costs.

The important point is that inventories can absorb supply disruptions only temporarily. As disruptions persist, the market will increasingly have to rebalance through higher prices and demand destruction.

The world has already used a substantial part of its protection against supply shocks. The next disruption will trigger a much sharper repricing in oil than the previous ones.
